title: Rational marked inputs and controlled histories with boundary births
statement:
A rational input for a controlled marked-ideal history consists of an embedded ambient $S$ and marked ideal $M$ of [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation], over $k=\mathbf Q$, with ambient $Z=S.Z$, support $N=M.N$, inclusion $j$, ordered boundary $E$, coherent ideal $I$ [pqf-def-coherent] and positive mark $b$. The smooth structure maps [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and closed inclusion [def-weil-closed-immersion] are those already recorded; both structure maps are finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Each boundary member and its restriction to $N$ is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], and each boundary hypersurface is smooth over $\mathbf Q$. Ordered SNC and transversality are the adapted-center predicates [def-per-adapted-normal-crossings-center] for the bottom ideal on $Z$ and $N$, respectively, using regular systems of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. No Hilbert--Samuel presentation condition, irreducibility, connectedness, equidimensionality or nonemptiness is required. Cosupport on $N$ is the inverse image under $j$ of the existing ambient marked cosupport, equivalently $\operatorname{ord}_xI\ge b$ [def-trf-marked-ideal-order]. Maximal order means $\operatorname{ord}_xI=b$ at every cosupport point.

A controlled history step uses an admissible-blowup $\operatorname{Step}$ and its $\operatorname{Transforms}$ relation from [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation], admissible for the marked cosupport, using the actual ambient blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] and strict support transform [def-nagata-strict-transform], with invertible exceptional ideal on the transformed support. Retain its support map and center factorization through the old support, pinned by their commuting triangles with the closed immersion. A finite history consists of these inputs and steps, with a birth stage for every ordered boundary member: original members are born at zero, inherited members keep their birth, and each new exceptional member is born at its stage. An extension preserves all preceding inputs, steps and births. A smooth history pullback consists of stagewise smooth ambient maps over $\mathbf Q$, the existing marked-pullback relation and its cartesian support maps, pulled-back ordered boundaries and centers, commuting step diagrams and identical births. No constant-relative-dimension restriction is imposed; empty pulled-back centers are retained. An equivalence of histories consists of stagewise ambient isomorphisms over $\mathbf Q$ preserving the ordered boundaries, centers, diagrams and births; transport the second marked data by the existing marked-pullback relation and require the existing depth-wise $\operatorname{Equivalent}$ relation on each common ambient. In particular cosupports agree after every finite test depth, with existence of all transforms; this reuses the admissible, affine-line-product [def-sbc-affine-space] and exceptional-intersection tests of [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation], rather than defining a second test calculus.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; the precise definitions are BMT arXiv:0905.3580, sections 5.1--5.2, pp.9--10, full text read at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0905.3580.
